Title: Dual-specificity phosphatase 6 predicts the sensitivity of progestin therapy for atypical endometrial hyperplasia.

Journal/Date: Gynecologic oncology (2015)

MeSH Keywords: Antineoplastic Agents, Hormonal, Biomarkers, Cell Line, Tumor, Drug Resistance, Neoplasm, Dual Specificity Phosphatase 6, Endometrial Hyperplasia, Endometrial Neoplasms, Female


--- ABSTRACT ---
[OBJECTIVE]: We previously found that Dual-specificity phosphatase 6 (Dusp6) over-expression enhanced the growth-promoting effect of estrogen in endometrial adenocarcinoma cells. The aim of this study was to explore the correlation of Dusp6 expression with progestin sensitivity in atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) and earlier endometrial carcinomas (EC).
[METHODS]: Using immunohistochemistry study, we analyzed the expression of Dusp6 protein in AEH.
[RESULTS]: We found that progestin treatment was effective in 89% of AEH and 50% of EC. Before treatment, Dusp6 expression was significantly higher in progestin-sensitive AEH groups compared with progestin-resistant groups. After treatment, Dusp6 expression was significantly upregulated in progestin-sensitive groups, but not in progestin-resistant groups. Moreover, a high-dose of Dusp6 transfection significantly enhanced progestin-induced growth-inhibition in Ishikawa cells.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Dusp6 could be a predicting marker for deciding the effectiveness of progestin therapy in AEH.

Title: Dusp6 immunohistochemistry is associated with the response of atypical endometrial hyperplasia and early endometrial cancer to conservative treatment.

Journal/Date: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics (2022)

MeSH Keywords: Carcinoma, Endometrioid, Conservative Treatment, Dual Specificity Phosphatase 6, Endometrial Hyperplasia, Endometrial Neoplasms, Female, Humans, Immunohistochemistry


--- ABSTRACT ---
[OBJECTIVE]: Dual-specificity phosphatase 6 (Dusp6) was proposed as a predictive marker of response of atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) and early endometrial cancer (EEC) to conservative treatment. However, its predictive accuracy has never been calculated. We aimed to define it in conservatively treated AEH and EEC.
[METHODS]: All patients <45 years with AEH or EEC and conservatively treated with hysteroscopic resection + LNG-IUD insertion from 2007 to 2018 were retrospectively assessed. Dusp6 immunohistochemical expression was assessed and dichotomized as "strong" vs "weak". Relative risk (RR) for "no regression" and "recurrence" or AEH/EEC was calculated. Predictive accuracy was calculated as sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV) and area under the curve (AUC) on receiver operating characteristic curve.
[RESULTS]: Thirty-six women were included. Weak Dusp6 immunohistochemical expression was significantly associated with increased risk of resistance to treatment, with a RR = 16 (P = 0.0074); predictive accuracy analysis showed sensitivity = 80%, specificity = 90%, PPV = 57.1%, NPV = 96.4%, AUC = 0.85. A weak Dusp6 expression was not significantly associated with the risk of recurrence after an initial regression (RR = 0.4; P = 0.53).
[CONCLUSION]: Weak Dusp6 expression appears as a significant predictor of resistance of AEH/EEC to fertility-sparing treatment, with moderate predictive accuracy. Weak Dusp6 expression is significantly associated with resistance of atypical endometrial hyperplasia or early endometrial cancer to fertility-sparing treatment, with moderate predictive accuracy.

key_findings.finding: Direct human predictive evidence exists in a 2015 study (PMID 25451692; Gynecologic Oncology) of atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) and earlier endometrial carcinoma treated with progestin. DUSP6 protein was measured by immunohistochemistry; progestin was effective in 89% of AEH and 50% of carcinoma. Pretreatment DUSP6 expression was significantly higher in progestin-sensitive AEH than resistant AEH, and DUSP6 increased after treatment in sensitive but not resistant groups. Thus, higher baseline DUSP6 predicted response/sensitivity, while failure to upregulate DUSP6 during treatment tracked resistance. The abstract does not specify the progestin agent, cohort size, quantitative effect estimate, or DOI.

Independent search record for the same primary study

key_findings.finding: A second retrospective human validation/accuracy study (PMID 34837386; International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics, 2022) included 36 women younger than 45 with AEH or early endometrial cancer treated from 2007–2018 by hysteroscopic resection plus a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device. Pretreatment DUSP6 immunohistochemistry was dichotomized as strong versus weak. Weak DUSP6 was associated with treatment resistance/no regression (RR 16, P=0.0074), with sensitivity 80%, specificity 90%, PPV 57.1%, NPV 96.4%, and AUC 0.85. Weak DUSP6 was not associated with recurrence after initial regression (RR 0.4, P=0.53). This supports predictive value for initial response/treatment failure, not prognostic prediction of relapse.

key_findings.finding: Mechanistic support comes from a human endometrial adenocarcinoma Ishikawa-cell study (PMID 23419500; Molecular and Cellular Endocrinology, 2013), not a clinical AEH/EIN cohort. DUSP6 overexpression blocked FGF2-induced MAPK/ERK1/2 signaling, enhanced estrogen-induced cell growth, and progesterone reduced growth approximately twofold both with and without forced DUSP6 expression. This demonstrates pathway/cell-growth biology relevant to hormone response but does not establish DUSP6 as a clinical predictor of progestin response.

key_findings.finding: The available evidence is concentrated in two human studies and is supportive but limited: both evaluate DUSP6 protein by immunohistochemistry, and the 2022 study uses LNG-IUD therapy; the 2015 abstract does not identify the progestin. Evidence supports DUSP6 as a predictive-response biomarker for AEH/closely related early endometrial cancer, with low/weak expression indicating higher risk of initial treatment failure. It does not support DUSP6 as a recurrence prognostic marker after regression, and no direct evidence of DUSP6-specific prediction in formally designated EIN cohorts was identified in the searches.
